title: POC scoping: quality eval plan with Halcyon Med
next_steps: Send POC plan + pricing sheet by 2026-03-16
Share security docs (SOC2/ISO) and network diagram
Schedule 2-hour benchmark run for week of 2026-03-23
Provide golden prompt set and annotation rubric
action_items: Jordan Lee: send POC plan and pricing (due 2026-03-16)
Priya Sharma: prepare benchmark config and Docker image (due 2026-03-20)
Sara Park: share sample dataset and HIPAA constraints (due 2026-03-17)
Dr. Mark Chen: confirm evaluation stakeholders and success criteria (due 2026-03-18)
summary: AE + SE ran a POC scoping call with Halcyon Medical focused on defining a quality evaluation plan: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks, scoring approach, and timelines. Customer emphasized HIPAA/PHI constraints, desire for repeatable benchmarks, and clear pass/fail criteria tied to product rollout. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send POC plan and pricing, SE to prepare benchmark image/config, customer to share sample data and confirm stakeholders.
topics: Quality evaluation: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for making time. i'm jordan from redwood, i'll kick us off. we have priya here from the se team. quick intro?
[00:14] Dr. Mark Chen: thanks jordan, mark here, cto at halcyon medical, joined by sara and luis. we want to scope a poc to validate quality on our triage/summary workflow.
[00:28] Jordan Lee: perfect, high level - we want to align on success criteria, what dataset to use, the golden prompts, and how we score hallucination and format fidelity.
[00:40] Priya Sharma: just to set expectations, our typical poc has two parts: functional quality eval (golden prompts, regression tests) and a performance benchmark (latency, throughput). both should run reproducibly.
[00:52] Sara Park: hi - our main constraint is PHI/HIPAA, so we need either private deployment or strong encryption + audit logs. we also want to make sure the model doesn't hallucinate patient data.
[01:06] Jordan Lee: noted. for scopes like this we usually provide a small dockerized benchmark harness plus a notebook to run golden prompts and scoring. priya, i'll let you explain the quality eval plan.
[01:18] Priya Sharma: sure. proposed approach: we define a golden prompt set ~200 items representing triage and discharge summary prompts. those are hand-curated by halcyon SMEs. we run model variants (hosted open models, and a dedicated/quantized variant) and collect outputs. scoring will be multi-dimensional: correctness (factual accuracy), hallucination rate, format compliance (structured fields present), and a utility score from human raters.
[01:44] Luis Gomez: 200 seems fine, can we also include ~50 adversarial prompts to test edge cases?
[01:50] Priya Sharma: yes - we usually reserve 10-20% as adversarial/regression prompts. good for early detection of regressions.
[02:00] Dr. Mark Chen: what do you mean by hallucination rate exactly? how do you measure it?
[02:06] Priya Sharma: good question. two parts: automatic detectors for hallucination (keyword checks, entity mismatches vs. ground truth) plus a human annotation pass. we calculate hallucination rate = (# outputs with unsupported facts) / (total outputs) and set threshold e.g., <2% for pass.
[02:24] Jordan Lee: and format compliance - we define a strict schema for summaries (fields: summary_text, ood_flags, recommended_action) and compute format pass rate. the POC acceptance could require >95% format compliance.
[02:36] Sara Park: we also need to check that PHI isn't introduced. sometimes models invent names or ids. is that covered?
[02:43] Priya Sharma: yes, we add PHI hallucination checks: regex detectors for MRN/SSN patterns, name-entity overlap with patient list, and human spot checks. outputs that include realistic-seeming PHI where none should exist count as critical failures.
[02:58] Jordan Lee: on workload sizing, what's your expected qps and latency SLOs?
[03:03] Luis Gomez: for the pilot, peak is about 15 qps with 1-3 tokens/sec per user? actually we expect average 6 qps with p95 latency under 700ms for short summaries (<=512 tokens).
[03:18] Priya Sharma: ok that's helpful. for the benchmark we'll configure dedicated instances to meet 15 qps and measure p50/p95/p99 latencies. we'll also run a concurrency sweep to find optimal batch sizes and KV cache impact.
[03:33] Dr. Mark Chen: can we measure cost per 1k tokens during the benchmark so we can compare hosted vs dedicated?
[03:39] Jordan Lee: yes we'll report unit economics - tokens/cost, and also perf/cost curves across quantization and batch sizes.
[03:46] Sara Park: timeline? we need results before product review on 2026-04-15.
[03:51] Jordan Lee: realistic timeline: 
- 2026-03-16: POC plan + pricing and security docs delivered (jordan)
- 2026-03-17: customer shares sanitized sample dataset and success criteria (sara)
- 2026-03-20: se provides benchmark config + docker image (priya)
- 2026-03-23: run 2-hour benchmark and initial quality eval
- 2026-03-30: deliver final report and recommendations
[04:20] Luis Gomez: that fits our calendar. on the scoring approach, can you walk through the rubric?
[04:26] Priya Sharma: rubric draft: correctness score (0-3), hallucination binary flag per response, format flag (pass/fail), utility rating 1-5 by annotators. final composite score = weighted sum: 40% correctness, 30% utility, 20% format, 10% hallucination penalty. thresholds: composite >= 3.5/5 for pass.
[04:48] Dr. Mark Chen: weights make sense, but we need to see examples. can you provide sample annotations?
[04:54] Priya Sharma: yes we'll attach an annotation guideline doc and 10 gold-labeled examples. we also recommend 3 independent annotators per response to reduce subjectivity.
[05:06] Jordan Lee: about regression tests - we propose a regression suite of 100 prompts that must not degrade across model releases. we run that suite nightly for the POC on the dedicated env.
[05:18] Sara Park: nightly sounds good but for the POC we just need a one-off proof and a simple automation to rerun the regression before handoff.
[05:27] Priya Sharma: fair - we'll set up a simple script that runs the suite and outputs pass/fail and a regression diff.
[05:34] Luis Gomez: what about prompt stability? we plan to tune prompts - how do we ensure tuned prompts don't overfit to the golden set?
[05:41] Priya Sharma: we separate tune set vs holdout evaluation set. tuning can use half the golden prompts; evaluation uses the holdout plus new ad hoc prompts. we capture prompt templates and versions to ensure repeatability.
[05:54] Jordan Lee: any thoughts about private deployment vs hosted for the POC? customer needs PHI protections.
[06:00] Dr. Mark Chen: ideal is private (VPC) deployment in our cloud account. but if hosted with dedicated tenancy and envelope encryption + KMS keys we might accept that for the pilot, provided audit logs and SOC2 evidence.
[06:16] Priya Sharma: we can do both: Redwood Private (VPC) or a Dedicated-hosted with customer-managed KMS. we'll list the tradeoffs in the doc - time-to-run is usually faster on hosted-dedicated, private VPC takes additional network setup (~5 business days).
[06:31] Sara Park: what about data retention and logs? we cannot have logs with full PHI retained longer than 30 days, and logs must be redacted.
[06:39] Jordan Lee: we'll include retention and redaction config in the security appendix. we support configurable retention and automatic redaction for known PHI patterns.
[06:47] Luis Gomez: benchmark metrics - besides latency and tokens, can we capture hallucination rate per prompt type and format pass rate per schema field?
[06:56] Priya Sharma: yes, breakdowns by prompt category, entity type, and edge-case buckets. we also produce per-model confusion matrices for common entities.
[07:06] Dr. Mark Chen: ok good. one more: can we run an automated hallucination detector? manual annotation is costly.
[07:13] Priya Sharma: we have heuristics - entity mismatch, contradiction detection vs patient record, numeric inconsistency checks. they catch a portion of hallucinations; human review needed for the rest. a combined approach works well: auto-filter likely hallucinations and prioritize human review on those.
[07:28] Jordan Lee: any objections to the pass thresholds i suggested earlier? hallucination <2%, format >95%, composite >=3.5.
[07:36] Sara Park: hallucination target might be aggressive; can we do <5% for pilot and tighten later?
[07:42] Dr. Mark Chen: agree with sara - for pilot let's accept <5%, but we'll require no critical PHI hallucinations.
[07:49] Priya Sharma: noted - we'll record both actual and target thresholds in the plan.
[07:54] Luis Gomez: what about tooling - how are outputs stored for annotation?
[07:58] Priya Sharma: bench harness outputs to S3 (or customer's storage for VPC), we provide an export with golden prompt id, response, model config, latency, and auto-tags. annotation UI is optional; we can accept CSV for manual annotation.
[08:12] Jordan Lee: let's talk about golden prompts generation - sara, you'll curate initial set?
[08:17] Sara Park: yes we'll pull 200 representative triage/discharge examples, annotate expected fields. we may need help to redact PHI.
[08:25] Priya Sharma: we'll provide a template for prompt + expected schema and a small guide for redaction.
[08:31] Dr. Mark Chen: on reporting - can you include examples of fail cases and suggested mitigations?
[08:36] Jordan Lee: yes final report will include per-prompt failures, aggregate metrics, recommended model variant and quantization settings, and operational recommendations (batching, cache TTLs).
[08:47] Luis Gomez: if we see a high hallucination rate, do you support interventions like retrieval augmentation?
[08:52] Priya Sharma: yes we can evaluate retrieval-augmented approaches in scope but that expands the POC. we can include a small RAG experiment if you want - maybe a 1-day add-on.
[09:02] Sara Park: let's keep RAG optional for now; if basic model doesn't meet thresholds we'll revisit.
[09:08] Jordan Lee: any compliance docs needed now? sara asked for SOC2 and ISO attestation plus network diagram. we'll attach those.
[09:16] Sara Park: also, can you confirm if model outputs are mutable by Redwood staff? we need assurance for data sovereignty.
[09:22] Priya Sharma: no, for Dedicated/Private deployments data access policies are customer-controlled; Redwood has no access unless explicitly granted. we'll capture that in the security appendix.
[09:33] Dr. Mark Chen: ok sounds good. final questions?
[09:38] Luis Gomez: just one - scoring aggregation: you mentioned 3 annotators; do you take median or mean?
[09:43] Priya Sharma: we use median for ordinal scores to reduce outlier impact, mean for continuous metrics. we'll document the exact aggregation formula.
[09:51] Jordan Lee: recap of next steps - jordan sends plan + pricing (03/16), priya sends docker/bench (03/20), halcyon provides data (03/17), schedule benchmark week of 03/23. any other items?
[10:05] Sara Park: please also include the annotation rubric and the 10 gold examples.
[10:09] Jordan Lee: will do. thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[10:13] Dr. Mark Chen: thanks, bye.
[10:15] End of recording.
